w: Built in 1869 as the Yeni Cami mosque, replacing a church destroyed in Heraklion's 1856 earthquake, this eclectic square-plan temple with a dome and stone-carved apse returned to Christian worship in 1925. In 2013 it was declared a cathedral of the Archdiocese of Crete, dedicated to Saint Titus.
s: Mosque turned church turned cathedral, in one building
_facts: Built 1869 as the Yeni Cami mosque, after an 1856 earthquake destroyed the earlier church
Converted back to Christian worship in 1925

w: Seat of the Archbishop of Crete, this Greek Orthodox cathedral is dedicated to Saint Menas, a martyr and wonderworker who died around 309 AD and became Heraklion's patron saint. Its full Greek title, Hierós Metropolitikós Naós Hagíou Mena, translates literally as Saint Menas' Cathedral.
s: Cathedral of Crete's Archbishop, named for the patron saint
_facts: Greek Orthodox cathedral, seat of the Archbishop of Crete
Dedicated to Saint Menas (285-309 AD), patron saint of Heraklion
Name translates literally as Saint Menas' Cathedral

w: A Minoan cemetery on a hill above Archanes, used from around 2400 BC to 1200 BC. Discovered in 1957 and excavated for 25 years from 1965 by Yiannis Sakellarakis, its 6,600 sq m necropolis holds 26 funerary buildings of varying shapes, making it one of the most complete Minoan burial sites found on Crete.
s: Minoan necropolis excavated over 25 years near Archanes
_facts: Minoan cemetery in use from roughly 2400 BC to 1200 BC
6,600 sq m necropolis with 26 funerary buildings
Discovered 1957, excavated over 25 years from 1965 by Yiannis Sakellarakis
Visible from Mount Juktas; reached via a signed path from Archanes

w: Built in 1239 under Venetian rule as a Roman Catholic basilica, it became the Defterdar Ahmet Pasha Mosque after the 1669 Ottoman conquest and served as one until 1915. Restored after 1956, this Gothic three-aisled basilica is now a public art gallery, one of few former Catholic churches still standing in Crete.
s: Venetian basilica, then mosque, now an art gallery
_facts: Built 1239 during Venetian rule as a Roman Catholic basilica
Converted into the Defterdar Ahmet Pasha Mosque after the 1669 Ottoman conquest
Used as a mosque until 1915; restored after 1956
Now a public art gallery; one of few former Catholic churches standing in Crete

w: In Myrtia village, 20 km south of Heraklion, this museum is devoted to the life and work of Nikos Kazantzakis, a nine-time Nobel Prize in Literature candidate best known worldwide for Zorba the Greek and The Last Temptation of Christ.
s: Village museum for the author of Zorba the Greek
_facts: Located in Myrtia village, 20 km south of Heraklion
Dedicated to writer Nikos Kazantzakis
Kazantzakis was a nine-time Nobel Prize in Literature candidate
Author of Zorba the Greek and The Last Temptation of Christ

w: Built for ceremonial purposes in the 15th century BC at the heart of the Bronze Age palace of Knossos, this chamber is considered the oldest throne room in Europe. Knossos was one of the main centres of Minoan civilisation, and the room sits within the palatial complex most closely tied to that culture.
s: The oldest throne room in Europe, inside Knossos palace
_facts: Ceremonial chamber built in the 15th century BC
Considered the oldest throne room in Europe
Located within the Bronze Age palace of Knossos, a major Minoan civilisation centre

w: Officially Eleftheriou Venizelou Square, named for the Cretan statesman, this Venetian-era plaza is far better known by its popular name, after the Morosini Fountain at its centre, called 'the Lions' because four lions support its main basin.
s: Venetian square nicknamed for its four-lion fountain
